title: The Prestige
events_chronological: As young shills, Robert Angier and Alfred Borden plant themselves in the audience for the magician Milton, with Angier's wife Julia performing the water-tank escape.
Borden ties the wrong knot before the escape and Julia drowns in front of the audience.
Angier blames Borden, and their feud costs Borden two fingers when Angier sabotages his bullet catch.
Borden debuts The Transported Man, stepping into one cabinet and out of another across the stage in an instant.
Angier hires a drunk lookalike, Root, to reproduce the trick, and Borden wrecks the act by taking Root's place beneath the stage.
Angier sends his assistant Olivia to spy on Borden, and she falls in love with him instead.
Olivia brings Angier Borden's coded diary, and Borden supplies the keyword knowing she will pass it on.
The diary sends Angier across America to Colorado Springs to find Nikola Tesla.
Tesla builds Angier a machine that does not transport but duplicates, and Angier tests it on his hat and on a cat.
Tesla is driven out of Colorado and leaves the machine behind with a written warning to drown it in the sea.
Angier stages The Real Transported Man, drowning the copy left under the stage at every single performance.
Borden sneaks beneath the stage on the hundredth night and watches Angier drown in a locked water tank.
Borden is convicted of Angier's murder, held in Newgate reading Angier's diary, and stripped of custody of his daughter.
Lord Caldlow, who is Angier alive and in disguise, buys Borden's secrets and takes the child.
Cutter delivers the machine to Caldlow's theatre and realises who Caldlow really is.
Borden's twin, who has shared his name and his life all along, shoots Angier in the theatre and takes his daughter back.
Angier dies on the floor among the tanks holding every copy of himself he has drowned.
syuzhet_notes: The film nests two diaries inside each other. Told-order bullets 1-2 are the present, Borden in his cell; bullets 3, 11 and 12 come out of Angier's Colorado journal, which Borden is reading; and bullets 4-10 come out of Borden's own journal, which Angier is reading inside that journal - a flashback two levels deep. Told-order bullet 1 is also a flash-forward relative to almost everything that follows, since the drowning it opens on happens near the end of the story.
fabula_notes: That Borden has always been two men sharing one identity is the film's withheld premise, so every Borden bullet before the last two silently describes whichever twin was on duty that day. Which twin hangs and which survives is left for the audience to work out, and Angier's drowned duplicates accumulate off screen between performances.
